title: Add release-branch scheduler smoke tests for queueing/backpressure/load-shedding regressions
creator: Connor O'Brien
description:
Backports to LTS/release branches are repeatedly regressing the scheduler in ways that don’t show up in unit tests or the broader perf suite until late (or worse: in pilot). We need a small set of targeted, deterministic smoke tests that run on every release branch PR and on the patch RC build to catch the common failure modes: (1) queue buildup / head-of-line blocking, (2) backpressure propagation issues, (3) load-shedding correctness and fairness under overload.

Scope: add a new CI workflow for release branches (and optionally main) that executes a short “scheduler smoke” suite with fixed seeds and bounded runtime.

Why now: LTS patch cadence + reduced change window means we can’t afford to discover scheduler pathologies during RC perf gates. These are correctness/reliability issues that should be caught before artifacts are produced.

Primary owner: Scheduling (Sofia). QA automation + Release Eng to help wire into release-branch workflows.

Non-goals: replacing the full perf-canary benchmarks; these tests should be fast, deterministic, and focused on scheduler behavior.
acceptance_criteria: New smoke test suite runs in CI for release branches (runtime-*-lts and release/*) on every PR and nightly cron
Suite completes in <= 12 minutes on standard CI runners; failure output includes a single summary line + a link/attachment to artifacts

Covers 3 scenarios with deterministic inputs: (1) mixed prompt lengths + continuous batching enabled, (2) overload with backpressure + queue limit enforcement, (3) load-shedding when at/over configured max inflight (ensures shed rate + no starvation for small requests)
Produces machine-readable metrics artifact (json) with: enqueue latency p50/p95, time-in-queue, shed_count, shed_reason breakdown, starvation indicator (max wait time for short requests)
Flake rate < 1% across 30 runs (tracked in CI); if noisy, tests must have a documented stabilization plan (fixed seed, warmup phase, fewer moving parts)
Release managers can reference this suite as a required gate in the LTS patch runbook
implementation_notes:
Proposed design:
- Harness: lightweight integration test runner that spins up the scheduler + a stubbed “execution backend” (no GPU required). We simulate token generation time with deterministic sleeps / event loop ticks to model long vs short requests.
- Determinism: fixed random seed, fixed scenario definitions, no wall-clock assertions other than upper bounds; prefer logical time progression where possible.
- Assertions: thresholds defined relative to baseline within the test (e.g., short requests should not exceed X * median long request queue time). Avoid absolute latency thresholds that vary by runner.
- Metrics collection: export scheduler internal counters/timers via existing debug endpoint (or add a test-only metrics sink).

Scenarios:
1) Mixed-length fairness: 80% short prompts, 20% long prompts. Ensure short requests do not starve when long prompts saturate batches.
2) Backpressure propagation: downstream “backend” slows; scheduler should reduce admit rate, enforce max queue length, and not exceed configured inflight.
3) Load-shedding under overload: send burst > 3x capacity; validate shedding occurs for lowest-priority queue first (or per configured policy), and shed reasons are correct.

CI wiring:
- Add workflow: .github/workflows/release-branch-scheduler-smoke.yml
- Triggers: pull_request on release/* and runtime-*-lts branches; workflow_dispatch; nightly schedule for active release branches
- Artifacts: upload metrics.json + a short text summary; annotate PR with pass/fail + key metrics deltas if available

Open question: Do we also run on main? Recommendation: yes, but do not block merges until we’ve proven stability for ~2 weeks.
progress_updates: 2025-02-10 (Sofia): Drafted scenario definitions + initial harness plan. Aligning with Marcus on metric names so they’re consistent with perf-canary outputs.
2025-02-12 (Leila): QA can provide a minimal runner wrapper + junit output so failures are readable in CI. Need final list of assertions per scenario.
2025-02-14 (Sahana): Release-branch workflow template exists from ENG-4824; can add an additional job gated on branch name. Please keep runtime <= 15 min to avoid blocking patch week.
2025-02-18 (Sofia): Implemented scenario 1 + 2 locally; seeing intermittent variance when using wall-clock sleeps. Switching to logical time ticks in the stub backend.
comments: Connor O'Brien (2025-02-07): Marking P0 for LTS. We’ve had multiple close calls where scheduler regressions were discovered during RC perf gates, which is too late in the LTS process. These should be correctness-style tests with deterministic pass/fail.

Sean Gallagher (2025-02-08): +1. For Dedicated/Private, backpressure issues show up as cascading latency and error budget burn. Please include a clear signal for “queue growth is unbounded” and make sure the suite fails fast when invariants are violated.

Marcus Reed (2025-02-10): If you can output a compact metrics.json with consistent keys, we can ingest it later into the perf gate summary artifact. Don’t overfit to any single GPU runner; relative assertions are safer.

Sofia Ivanova (2025-02-11): For load-shedding: we should assert both (a) shed happens when limits are exceeded and (b) we don’t shed requests that have already been admitted unless policy says so. We’ve regressed this in the past during refactors.

Rafael Mendes (2025-02-13): Please add a one-pager in the failure output explaining likely causes (e.g., inflight accounting mismatch, queue limit ignored, starvation). During patch week, on-call needs quick triage guidance.
Leila Farouk (2025-02-16): Suggest we make these junit tests with structured attachments; otherwise failures get lost in logs. I can help wire artifacts + summary formatting.
next_steps: Stabilize stub backend to remove wall-clock variance (logical ticks)
Finalize pass/fail assertions and thresholds per scenario (review with SRE)
Land CI workflow and ensure it triggers correctly on release branches
Add short triage notes to failure output + link to internal doc section
Track flake rate for 2 weeks; only then consider making it merge-blocking on main
